title: Residual Connections & Layer Normalization — Track the Residual Stream
key_insight: Initialization, normalization, and sometimes explicit residual scaling keep branch updates proportionate to the stream. Measure activation norms by layer to find drift.
body:
## Track the Residual Stream

Many blocks write updates into one continuing vector stream. If update scales grow unchecked, later layers receive an unstable mixture.

Initialization, normalization, and sometimes explicit residual scaling keep branch updates proportionate to the stream. Measure activation norms by layer to find drift.

Layer norm behaves similarly at training and inference because it uses each token’s own features, unlike batch normalization’s batch statistics.
common_mistakes: Residual connections permanently skip every transformation.
Layer normalization averages unrelated users together.
Normalization removes all learned scale and shift.
mini_exercise: Draw “Track the Residual Stream” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: These support stable information and gradient flow through deep transformer stacks.
explain_back_prompt: Using “Track the Residual Stream,” explain Residual Connections & Layer Normalization without assuming the listener knows modern AI.
